findings.title: tethra track prints "Tracking verified" and exits 0 from a liveness-blind cached state
findings.reproduction: Run `tethra track .`; let one real request be observed; make the gateway unavailable (stop it, or remove the route/link) before the next 5s poll.
findings.expected: The headline and exit code reflect present-tense health, as `track status` does.
findings.actual: `check_traffic` switches on the cached `setup.state` column after a `GatewayLiveness::Unknown` refresh; `WatchStatus::Observed` prints "✓ Tracking verified" and returns Ok(()) = exit 0.
findings.root_cause: apps/cli/src/track_cmd.rs:726,745,758 gate on verify::check_traffic (crates/tracking/src/verify.rs:139-155), which calls state::refresh (state.rs:1015-1017) and discards .current. The derived ladder (state.rs:937-951) uses observed_ever, not liveness.
findings.evidence: The same file states the opposite rule at track_cmd.rs:993-999 ("Exit 0 only for a present-tense success"). The desktop fixed this exact defect and says so at apps/desktop/src/components/TrackFlow.tsx:394-400, gating on currently_working at :1095, with a regression test at TrackFlow.test.tsx:650-675.
findings.regression_coverage: None. apps/cli/tests/track.rs has 10 tests, all on the unconfigured path; no test exercises the verify loop or track status against a configured setup.
findings.required_remediation: Gate track_cmd.rs:745 and :758 on refresh_with(conn, &setup, liveness).current.is_currently_working(), as status() already does, and add a CLI regression test.

findings.title: The default dashboard renders a fabricated zero for providers that report no usage
findings.reproduction: Track a project using a provider whose manifest has usage_shape = "" (cohere, google-gemini, langsmith, replicate, supabase), make real requests, open the default Activity view.
findings.expected: Absent usage is a state, not a zero — as GatewayView already renders it.
findings.actual: apps/desktop/src/components/DashboardView.tsx:290-296 renders {summary.input_tokens} / {summary.output_tokens} and ${cost} unconditionally, so the user sees '0 / 0' and '$0.0000' after successful traffic.
findings.root_cause: usage_event_count is on the DTO (types.ts:1338) but never referenced in DashboardView.tsx; the guard exists only in GatewayView.tsx:1281-1288.
findings.evidence: Contradicts three written invariants: docs/activity-onboarding/PRODUCT_BEHAVIOR.md:272 ('Absent usage data is a state, never a silent zero'), docs/gateway/COVERAGE_LIMITATIONS.md:42 ('never a fabricated zero'), docs/decisions/0019-local-gateway.md:61 ('never a fabricated 0'). The PR makes Activity the default view. DashboardView.test.tsx:65 even sets usage_event_count: 0 in its fixture, and no assertion catches it.
findings.required_remediation: Apply the GatewayView.tsx:1281-1288 guard in DashboardView, and add an assertion for the usage_event_count == 0 case.

findings.title: Shipping documents and a UI string claim database tampering cannot redirect credentials
findings.reproduction: UPDATE gateway_routes SET provider_id='anthropic' WHERE route_prefix='openai'; then send a request to /openai/*.
findings.expected: Either the redirection is prevented, or no document claims it is.
findings.actual: crates/gateway/src/routes.rs:628-650 resolves a manifest route via providers::find(&provider_id) with provider_id read straight from the untrusted row; route_mac is verified only for custom rows (:696-716). /openai/* resolves to api.anthropic.com:443 with the OpenAI credential attached. 13 manifests declare a gateway origin.
findings.root_cause: provider_id, route_prefix and enabled are not bound into any authenticated state for manifest routes.
findings.evidence: docs/gateway/SECURITY.md:40-47 — heading 'Why database tampering cannot redirect your credentials', closing 'A same-user process editing SQLite cannot make /openai/... (with your key attached) go anywhere else.' Also docs/gateway/ARCHITECTURE.md:121-123 and the shipped UI string at apps/desktop/src/components/GatewayView.tsx:830-832. The correct exclusion exists at docs/activity-onboarding/SECURITY_AND_PRIVACY.md:306-327, and :337-339 even states the right position, so the repository contradicts itself. POST_FINAL_REAUDIT_REMEDIATION_MATRIX.md:182 records this as already done.
findings.regression_coverage: crates/gateway/tests/routes.rs:74 tests only an UNKNOWN provider id, which fails closed; a known id succeeds and is untested.
findings.required_remediation: Correct docs/gateway/SECURITY.md, docs/gateway/ARCHITECTURE.md and the GatewayView UI string to match SECURITY_AND_PRIVACY.md:306-327, and add a test for the known-id case. Optionally bind provider_id into the route MAC.
findings.note: SEC-01's disposition is accepted risk, and that acceptance depends on honest disclosure. The disclosure is contradicted in three shipping places including the desktop UI.

findings.title: The SEC-02 request-body deadline is per request, not per connection
findings.actual: body_deadline is computed at forward.rs:853 inside handle_request, which is called once per keep-alive iteration at forward.rs:463. A client completing slow bodies gets a fresh 300s each request and is never idle, so CLIENT_BODY_DEADLINE, CLIENT_BODY_IDLE_TIMEOUT and CLIENT_KEEPALIVE_IDLE all fail to fire.
findings.evidence: Measured: one connection held one of 128 slots for 422.06s across 20 slow-body requests. Falsifies KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md:281-287, SECURITY_AND_PRIVACY.md:352-357 and POST_FINAL_REAUDIT_REMEDIATION_MATRIX.md:194, which all state a ~360s bound.
findings.required_remediation: Re-disposition SEC-02 FIXED -> PARTIAL; hoist the deadline into serve_connection as a per-connection budget; correct the three documents.
findings.note: Availability only, loopback-only, 503 rather than queueing, no credential impact; an attacker able to open loopback connections is already on the machine.

findings.title: Two projects linking one .env destroys the user's original value and reports it restored
findings.reproduction: Create two differently-named projects on one folder, then `tethra track <dir> --project a` and `--project b`; undo a, then undo b.
findings.expected: Either refuse the second link, or restore the user's original value.
findings.actual: B records A's gateway URL as B's prior (priors keyed by link_slug, envlink.rs:616). A's undo hits LeftUserEdit, which outcome_is_settled treats as settled (envlink.rs:1418), so complete:true and A's link row is deleted; it also restores NO_PROXY away. B's undo then "restores" A's dead slug. The user's real value is permanently gone with every outcome reported as Restored.
findings.root_cause: No LinkWarning variant for "another project already links this file" (envlink.rs:289-328); LeftUserEdit classified as settled.
findings.evidence: diagnose cannot see it — env_drifted iterates report.links (diagnose.rs:74-96) and none remain. No credential reaches a wrong origin: an unknown slug 404s (forward.rs:168).
findings.required_remediation: Warn (or refuse) when another link row already covers the file; do not classify LeftUserEdit as settled when a prior was recorded.
findings.reachability_note: The CLI refuses the implicit form: two projects on one folder makes `tethra track <dir>` fail with "more than one project" (apps/cli/tests/track.rs:210-231), and apply.rs:864-885 adopts an existing project by name rather than duplicating. Requires deliberate --project overrides.

findings.title: tethra gateway install persists the port after starting the service; doctor and status cannot see the divergence
findings.root_cause: apps/cli/src/gateway_cmd.rs:409 installs before :419 save_config; the plist carries no --port, so the service reads store::port_hint (store.rs:46-49), which swallows every failure into None, and binds port 0 (gateway_cmd.rs:1062). serve_service_mode never persists the port it bound.
findings.evidence: Root cause of the one unexplained CI link failure (run 30413022801, head 9844c49): install took 13.38s vs ~0.5s, consistent with the full 10s identity-probe timeout at gateway_cmd.rs:431-446. Desktop (main.rs:2589-2599) and tracking apply (apply.rs:381-420) both persist first; only this path does not.
findings.required_remediation: Move save_config above lc.install; have serve_service_mode persist its bound port; add a doctor finding for config.port != gateway_status.port.
findings.note: The remediation classified this as a harness reliability defect; it is a product defect. Safe recovery exists (gateway restart) but doctor and status report the link healthy.

findings.title: Manifest binds check identities for 9 of 63 service-scope checks; 54 are count-bound
findings.evidence: My own forgery suite: renaming one APPLY check is ACCEPTED (case 2b), while the same edit to a SERVICE check is refused. full:foreground binds 0 of 57, offline:none 0 of 20.
findings.mitigation: enumerate_checks() proves the group table against the source, so a check cannot silently disappear; the register rejects duplicates, skips and informational substitution.
findings.required_remediation: Extend required_checks to every group, or introduce stable per-check IDs.

findings.title: Validation cleanup's bootout skips its ownership proof when the plist is absent
